You are a professional biblical lexicographer fluent in Spanish. Translate the following English lexicon entry into Spanish.

Lemma: H8199

ENGLISH GLOSSES TO TRANSLATE:
  Terse gloss: "To judge, govern, vindicate, contend at law; as participle: judge (office-holder); Niphal: be judged, stand trial"
  Readable gloss: "Shaphat is the legal and governmental verb of the Hebrew Bible — covering the full arc from courtroom adjudication to national governance to divine vindication of the oppressed. In the Judges period, the shofet was not merely an arbitrator but a charismatic military-political leader, a sense Arabic qada (spanning both 'judge' and 'rule') confirms. The same verb turns adversarial in the Niphal to mean 'enter into a lawsuit,' as when God challenges Israel to contend with Him (Isa 43:26). Spanish distinguishes juzgar (adjudicate) from gobernar (govern) and vindicar (vindicate), mapping the same fractures visible in the Hebrew evidence."

SENSES:
  Sense 1: "to judge, adjudicate"
    Enriched: The foundational Qal verbal action: judging, rendering verdicts, administering justice. Ninety-eight occurrences from Samuel judging Israel at Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah (1 Sam 7:16) to Solomon's prayer for judicial wisdom (1 Kgs 3:9). Arabic hakama, Spanish juzgar, French juger, and Korean simpanhada converge on forensic adjudication.
    Existing Spanish translations: Y-juzgó, juzgaré, te-juzgaré, y-juzgaba, y-juzgó
  Sense 2: "judge (person, office-holder)"
    Enriched: The Qal active participle lexicalized as the substantive 'judge' (shofet/shoftim). Sixty-one occurrences spanning judicial appointment (Deut 16:18), the divine title 'Judge of all the earth' (Gen 18:25), and the era's named officeholders. Arabic al-qadi, Spanish el juez, and German der Richter confirm fully nominalized status.
    Existing Spanish translations: a-jueces, el-juez, jueces, juez, los-jueces
  Sense 3: "to vindicate, do justice for"
    Enriched: Qal forms with benefactive or vindicatory force: judging on behalf of, championing the oppressed. Sixteen occurrences including David's plea 'Judge me, O LORD' (Ps 7:8), 'Vindicate me, O God' (Ps 26:1), and Isaiah's call to 'judge the fatherless' (Isa 1:17). Arabic ihkum li ('judge for me') and Spanish juzgame confirm the pro-plaintiff orientation.
    Existing Spanish translations: Juzgará, Júzgame, Para-juzgar, defended, hacen-justicia, juzga, juzga-, juzgando, júzgame, que-juzga, y-me-hará-justicia
  Sense 4: "to enter into judgment, contend"
    Enriched: Niphal and related forms of reciprocal judicial action: entering a lawsuit, contending at law, litigating. Thirteen occurrences including God's 'I will enter into judgment with you' (Ezek 20:35–36), the futility of contending with God (Job 9:15), and the fool's courtroom (Prov 29:9). Arabic haakama (Form III, 'to litigate') marks the shift from authority to adversarial engagement.
    Existing Spanish translations: Y-me-juzgaré, a-mi-juez, entraré-en-juicio, entremos-en-juicio, juzgando, litigaré, litigué, que-juzga, quien-juzgue, y-juzgaré, y-litigaré
  Sense 5: "to rule, govern"
    Enriched: Qal extended from judicial to political governance — ruling or leading a people in the pre-monarchic pattern. Eleven occurrences: 'give us a king to judge us' meaning 'to govern us' (1 Sam 8:5–6), Moses sitting all day 'judging' as executive (Exod 18:13). Arabic qada with governance connotation and the book of Judges confirm shaphat as the pre-monarchic term for leadership.
    Existing Spanish translations: a-juzgar, juez, juez-de, para-juzgar, para-juzgarnos, y-nos-juzgará
  Sense 6: "to be judged (passive)"
    Enriched: The Niphal passive: to be judged, to stand trial, to undergo judgment. Five occurrences including 'let the nations be judged before you' (Ps 9:19), the assurance for the righteous (Ps 37:33), and the devastating 'when he is judged, let him come out guilty' (Ps 109:7). Arabic yudan and Korean simpan-batda confirm the passive voice.
    Existing Spanish translations: Cuando-sea-juzgado, cuando-juzgaba, cuando-sea-juzgado, sean-juzgadas, te-juzgarán
